web_sources.title: Foxglove Docs — Publish panel
web_sources.role_fact: The Publish panel sends messages on a topic back to the robotics stack.
web_sources.limitation: Publishing requires a live connection whose data source supports publishing; the panel does not supply a motion planner or execution policy.
web_sources.relevant_proposal: Borrow the pattern of an explicit command panel alongside the existing Three.js scene. Route commands through the application's validated backend contract.

web_sources.title: Foxglove Docs — Service Call panel
web_sources.role_fact: The Service Call panel sends a service request and displays the response.
web_sources.limitation: Service calls require a supporting live connection. A service response is distinct from completion of a long-running robot task.
web_sources.relevant_proposal: Use request and response visibility for diagnostics and configuration. Give long-running execution its own progress, cancellation, and terminal-result semantics.

web_sources.title: MoveIt Pro v10 Docs — Behavior Trees
web_sources.role_fact: An Objective is a top-level Behavior Tree for a complete robotic task; a Behavior is an action-node plugin executed within the Objective Server.
web_sources.limitation: Behavior Trees organize execution and state management; their adoption alone does not establish faster motion planning. Interfaces and implementation details from older product versions need separate verification.
web_sources.relevant_proposal: Adopt explicit task states, reusable steps, failure results, and recovery boundaries now. Consider a Behavior Tree runtime when branching recovery, retries, or reusable multi-step workflows outgrow the current executor.

web_sources.title: MoveIt Pro v10 Docs — Planners and Solvers
web_sources.role_fact: The documentation distinguishes ProRRT path planning, Cartesian planning, and PoseIK. PoseIK determinism is described as returning the same solution for the same input.
web_sources.limitation: Deterministic IK output is not a guarantee of fixed end-to-end planning latency. PoseIK optimize_distance intentionally searches for improvements for a configured time period.
web_sources.relevant_proposal: Separate IK, path search, collision validation, time parameterization, coordination search, and execution timing in measurements. Evaluate alternative solvers against representative workloads before changing the runtime.

web_sources.title: Rerun Docs — Embed Rerun in Web pages
web_sources.role_fact: The web viewer can open recorded RRD files or live SDK gRPC connections and can be embedded through an iframe or JavaScript package.
web_sources.limitation: The documented iframe approach lacks programmable viewer control. The JavaScript viewer package must be compatible with the SDK version that produced the data.
web_sources.relevant_proposal: Adopt a common time axis and live-versus-replay semantics in the existing UI. Add an embedded Rerun diagnostics view only if recording analysis would materially benefit; retain the primary Three.js interaction surface.

web_sources.title: Rerun Web Viewer v0.39.0 API — WebViewer
web_sources.role_fact: The inspected API includes time_update, timeline_change, and selection_change events, together with methods for setting the active timeline, current time, and playback state.
web_sources.limitation: These API facts were verified for v0.39.0. Viewer interaction events do not themselves define a robot command or execution interface.
web_sources.relevant_proposal: Use event-driven synchronization between diagnostics and the existing scene if embedding is adopted. Pin viewer and SDK versions and keep replay inspection separate from live execution commands.

web_sources.title: Isaac Lab Docs — Using a task-space controller
web_sources.role_fact: DifferentialIKController computes desired joint positions from a desired end-effector pose using the current pose, Jacobian, and joint positions; supported methods include damped least squares and pseudoinverse.
web_sources.limitation: The demonstrated IK controller computes joint targets. This alone does not establish collision-free whole-path planning through obstacles or the reliability of a learned policy.
web_sources.relevant_proposal: Borrow the separation between high-level action intent, control targets, and physics stepping. Consider Isaac Lab when policy learning, large-scale parallel learning environments, or its simulation features become explicit requirements.

web_sources.title: MoveIt Rolling Docs — Realtime Servo
web_sources.role_fact: Servo supports real-time joint or end-effector commands. Its collision and singularity checks scale down velocities near hazards, and collision checking is configurable.
web_sources.limitation: Velocity scaling and stopping are not a guarantee of finding a global route around an obstacle. Rolling command interfaces and configuration must be checked against the deployed MoveIt version.
web_sources.relevant_proposal: Keep collision-aware path planning for bin entry and exit. Consider Servo when visual feedback correction, teleoperation, or fine approach control becomes necessary and a suitable feedback/control loop exists.

web_sources.title: MoveIt Rolling Docs — Fuzzy-Matching Trajectory Cache Quickstart
web_sources.role_fact: The cache retrieves trajectories by fuzzy request matching and can rank candidates by planned execution time. The guide recommends repetitive non-dynamic motion and known starting poses.
web_sources.limitation: The documented default cache ignores collision and planning-scene constraints. A large start tolerance can return a trajectory whose first state differs substantially from the current robot state. A cache hit is not evidence that execution is valid in the current scene.
web_sources.relevant_proposal: Pilot validated reuse on repeated static segments. Check the current scene, trajectory constraints, current start state, and any connecting motion before execution; fall back to a fresh plan when validation fails.

web_sources.title: ROS rosdistro — Humble distribution manifest
web_sources.role_fact: At the inspection date, the Humble MoveIt release entry is 2.5.10-1 and its release-package list does not contain moveit_ros_trajectory_cache.
web_sources.limitation: This manifest describes the official distribution release and does not identify packages present in a particular source-built workspace. Documentation generated from main is not proof that a package is included in the stable Humble binary release.
web_sources.relevant_proposal: Inventory the deployed MoveIt version, source branch, and available packages before choosing a cache implementation. Do not assume a Rolling example can be installed unchanged in the current Humble environment.

web_sources.title: MoveIt — MoveIt 2 Source Build for Linux
web_sources.role_fact: The inspected installation page lists Humble among platforms currently supported by main and recommends distro branches for stable versions.
web_sources.limitation: The page explicitly describes main as an unstable API and says Humble support may be phased out once incompatible. Source-build feasibility does not guarantee compatibility with an existing workspace.
web_sources.relevant_proposal: Prefer the current stable deployment. If a needed feature requires main or a backport, evaluate it in isolation with pinned revisions and a representative compatibility test before changing the production workspace.

followup_ci.original_result: main workcell failed at HTTP capture start; original log did not preserve the HTTP rejection body
followup_ci.diagnosis: The diagnostic producer stopped publishing while one blocking start request prepared assets. A controlled 0.75-second input pause reproduced HTTP 400 with stale sensor readiness. This supports the failure path without proving the unrecorded original response body.
followup_ci.fix: One bounded HTTP request runs in a worker while the existing main loop alone pumps diagnostic input and ROS callbacks; no retries or production freshness relaxation. Bounded rejection status, path and body are retained.
